clue.text: Laugh and dance around with old-time movie star

indicators.note: one word placed around another surrounds it, holding it in its middle

blocks.note: the 1920s jazz-age dance
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film star of the past chuckles and does a little jig.
explanation.walkthrough: The dance is split after its first seven letters to wrap the laugh, so the star's surname emerges from the middle of the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Laughton was a British-American actor of the 1930s-50s, famous as Henry VIII and Captain Bligh.

clue.text: Weinberger tears up about army member in women's clothing

indicators.note: one word placed about another surrounds it on both sides

blocks.note: Caspar Weinberger, Reagan's Defense Secretary, was nicknamed Cap
tears up means rips
a soldier ant is one member of an ant army

explanation.surface: The former Defense Secretary is furious at a soldier in drag.
explanation.walkthrough: Army member suggests GI, but the army is of ants. The insect goes inside the tearing word before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri pants are close-fitting, calf-length trousers, popular women's wear since the 1950s.

clue.text: Entertain morning application

blocks.note: a.m. denotes morning hours
an application is a use

explanation.surface: A form to sign up for some morning entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse someone is to divert or delight them, a close synonym of entertain.

clue.text: Dilapidated mill taking lead with a personal care item

indicators.note: a dilapidated building has fallen apart, so the letters are reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crumbling mill full of lead pipes, plus some toiletry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' sounds like taking the front, but it is the metal, used by its chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip balm is a waxy salve for soothing chapped lips, a toiletry carried in a pocket.

clue.text: Harsh-sounding Shiva initially appearing with spear

indicators.note: initially points at the start, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: first letter of Shiva
a trident is a three-pronged spear, Shiva's emblem

explanation.surface: The Hindu god Shiva shows up, loudly, carrying his famous spear.
explanation.definitionFit: Strident describes a loud, grating sound or tone.

clue.text: Pacino's hole in one French region

blocks.note: Al Pacino's first name with the possessive
in golf, a hole in one is called an ace

explanation.surface: The actor Al Pacino sinks a hole in one while golfing in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Alsace is a historic region of north-eastern France bordering Germany.

clue.text: Linger suspiciously to conceal origin of malicious sprite

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it begins, its opening letter
something done suspiciously is shady and irregular, so the letters are jumbled
concealing something hides it within, so a letter goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of malicious

explanation.surface: Someone lurks shiftily to hide where a nasty imp came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Malicious sprite' reads as one definition, but malicious supplies only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A gremlin is an imaginary mischievous creature blamed for mechanical faults, a kind of sprite or imp.

clue.text: Boost oil by cloaking shadowy vehicle for Rush Limbaugh

indicators.note: a cloak wraps around its wearer, so one word surrounds another
in a down entry, to boost is to lift up, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
by and at both mean near, as in by or at the door
shadowy means dark

explanation.surface: Promoting oil through a shady outlet run by a conservative broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The shadowy word goes between the I and L of oil; the whole string is then read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Rush Limbaugh was the best-known American host of call-in political radio shows, his medium.

clue.text: Exposed shifting dune

indicators.note: something shifting moves around, so its letters change places

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Wind-blown sand has uncovered something.
explanation.definitionFit: Nude means naked, bare or uncovered.

clue.text: Try to acquire information about "large and chubby"

indicators.note: one word placed about another surrounds it on both sides

blocks.note: to pump someone is to question them for information
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Someone is fishing for gossip about a person described as large and chubby.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'large and chubby' look like a single description; only 'chubby' is the definition, with 'and' joining it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump is a mild synonym for chubby, describing a pleasantly rounded figure.

clue.text: Disgusted when eating a bit of seafood (like ghoti, perhaps)

indicators.note: a bit of a word is just a small part of it, here its opening letter
one thing eating another takes it inside, so a word swallows a letter

blocks.note: disgusted means repelled
first letter of seafood

explanation.surface: Someone is grossed out on eating a piece of seafood, perhaps a fish with an odd name.
explanation.walkthrough: GHOTI is George Bernard Shaw's famous joke spelling of FISH: GH as in enough, O as in women, TI as in nation. The S goes in after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghoti is the word fish spelled again using other English letter-sound pairs, so it is a respelled word.

clue.text: Nordic antelope uncovered mice on either side

indicators.note: with its cover taken off, a word loses its first and last letters
the same piece sits at both ends, before and after the middle word

blocks.note: mice without its outer letters, placed on the left
the eland is a large African antelope
the same stripped mice again, placed on the right

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian antelope sits with exposed mice beside it.
explanation.walkthrough: The stripped mice appear twice, once at each end of the antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceland is one of the Nordic countries, so anything Icelandic is Nordic.

clue.text: Heard storyteller's instrument…

indicators.note: something heard is taken by ear, so the word's sound matters, not its spelling

blocks.note: a storyteller in the sense of a fibber is a liar

explanation.surface: A bard's instrument is heard, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Storyteller is used in its sly sense of someone who tells tales, a liar. The ellipsis links the surface to the next clue but plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyre is a small harp-like stringed instrument from ancient Greece.

clue.text: Fruit of fragile transience

indicators.note: something fragile breaks easily, and a broken word is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A poetic phrase about the yield of life's brief, delicate passing.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectarines are smooth-skinned peaches, a stone fruit.

clue.text: …if playing, vocal involves a musical note

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap something in, so one word goes inside another

blocks.note: an actor playing Hamlet appears as Hamlet
vocal music is sung
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Continuing the lyre: if it is being played, a singer weaves in a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'If playing' reads as a unit, but 'if' alone is the definition. The note sits inside the vocal word after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Assuming works as a conjunction meaning on the supposition that, the same job as if.

clue.text: Hyena, e.g., is small coyote's principal nemesis

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
the principal or leading letter of coyote
Nemesis was the Greek goddess of retribution, an avenger

explanation.surface: A hyena is cast as the arch-enemy of a little coyote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' is the link, not a piece of wordplay. Principal means first.
explanation.definitionFit: A hyena is the classic example of a scavenger, an animal that feeds on carrion.

clue.text: Some poisoned gelato gets you nervous

indicators.note: some of a phrase is only part of it, so the answer is a run of its letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and into the second

explanation.surface: Eating ice cream that might be poisoned would make anyone jumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on edge is an idiom for being tense or anxious.

clue.text: Changing climates for climber

indicators.note: things changing take on a new form, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Shifting weather patterns affect a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Clematis is a flowering vine that grows up walls and trellises, a garden climbing plant.

clue.text: Cretan wobbling in a hypnotic state

indicators.note: something wobbling is unsteady and out of place, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man from Crete sways about under hypnosis.
explanation.definitionFit: A trance is a dazed, half-conscious condition such as hypnosis induces.

clue.text: It might contain water or fire, youngster

blocks.note: to can someone is slang for to fire them
a teen is a youngster

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what might hold water or fire, addressed to a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water or fire' look like a pair of elements; fire is a verb meaning dismiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen is a soldier's or hiker's flask for carrying drinking water.

clue.text: Bring to light medical precaution including uranium

indicators.note: one thing including another holds it within, so a letter is placed inside

blocks.note: a flu shot is a vaccination against influenza
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Revealing a doctor's preventive measure that contains radioactive uranium.
explanation.walkthrough: The U goes in after the O of the jab, not after the word flu.
explanation.definitionFit: To flush out is to drive someone or something from hiding into the open, exposing it.

clue.text: Warrior betrayed US airman, but not Navy

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for Navy

explanation.surface: A fighter double-crossed an American flier, though not a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: One N comes out of the airman's letters before they are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A samurai was a member of Japan's hereditary military class, a sword-bearing warrior.

clue.text: Lunatic raised Cain south of Massachusetts

in a down entry, south of puts one piece below the other

blocks.note: MA is the postal abbreviation for Massachusetts
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised Cain' is an idiom for making trouble, but here raised turns Cain upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A maniac is a person behaving wildly or insanely, a madman.

clue.text: Watched and listened to behavior likely to attract attention

blocks.note: making a scene is a public display of temper

explanation.walkthrough: 'Watched and listened to' looks like a pair of verbs to define together; only the first is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Seen is the past participle of see, so it means observed, as watched does.

clue.text: Cass Elliott, e.g., invested in doctor's old school

explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a medic but is a verb. The singer's title goes inside after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Alma mater, Latin for nourishing mother, is the school or college one attended.

clue.text: Rates, on the rise, converged on an irrational number

indicators.note: something rising goes upward, so in a down entry the word is read from the bottom

blocks.note: lines that converged met
pi is the best-known irrational number

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rates on the rise' reads like economics news; rates is a musical term.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempi is the plural of tempo, the speed at which a piece of music is played.

clue.text: I see a trace of beluga whale's pursuer

blocks.note: aha is an exclamation of sudden understanding
first letter of beluga

explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the beluga is a white whale, like Moby Dick.

taken as written

clue.text: Noodles, right? You said it!

clue.text: All you really need to hear Mr. MacGregor's child evaluate a kid

explanation.surface: Peter Rabbit's farmer has a child who sizes up a young goat, which is supposedly all you need.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'bairn assess a tease' runs into the phrase; the sounds blur across the joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare necessities are the minimum essentials for living, a phrase made famous by The Jungle Book song.
